modelIntro.title: Generate Kling 3.0 Videos From Text or Images
description: Kling AI Video Generator gives creators a direct way to test Kling 3.0 on Toolaze. Use text-to-video when you want to describe a complete scene from scratch, or image-to-video when a product, character, first frame, or visual style should guide the result.

Kling 3.0 is best used for cinematic movement, high-resolution visual drafts, short multi-shot sequences, and scenes where synchronized audio matters. In Toolaze, Kling 3.0 supports text or image input, up to 4 reference images, 3 to 15 second durations, 720p to 4K output options, and native audio at 720p or 1080p.

items.title: Kling 3.0
items.desc: Use Kling 3.0 for the broadest setup: 3 to 15 second clips, up to 4 reference images, 720p to 4K output, and native audio at 720p or 1080p.
items.prompt: Use it for polished social clips, product ads, storyboards, high-resolution drafts, and native-audio scenes.

items.title: Kling 3 Turbo
items.desc: Use Kling 3 Turbo when speed matters more than 4K. It supports 5 or 10 second clips, up to 2 reference images, 720p or 1080p output, and native audio.
items.prompt: Use it for prompt exploration, fast creative direction, and short scenes with sound cues.

items.title: Kling 2.6
items.desc: Use Kling 2.6 for reliable 5 or 10 second text-to-video or image-to-video clips with 720p or 1080p output and native audio support.
items.prompt: Use it for lower-credit Kling tests, simple storyboards, and audio-enabled drafts that do not need 4K.

items.title: Kling 2.5 Turbo Pro
items.desc: Use Kling 2.5 Turbo Pro for visual-only 1080p clips when you want a focused 5 or 10 second Kling pass without native audio.
items.prompt: Use it for motion checks, product movement, and straightforward visual iterations.

items.title: Kling 2.1 Master
items.desc: Use Kling 2.1 Master for older 1080p visual-only Kling generations when consistency matters more than using the newest model option.
items.prompt: Use it for controlled short clips and cases where the older Master option is preferred.

promptExamples.title: Kling AI Video Prompt Examples
promptExamples.subtitle: Use these four prompt structures to test motion, camera control, audio direction, and reference-guided generation.

items.title: Cinematic Product Reveal
items.prompt: A premium black smartwatch rests on a reflective glass surface. Slow 6-shot commercial sequence: macro crown detail, side profile, screen glow, strap texture, water droplets sliding off, final hero angle. Clean studio lighting, smooth dolly movement, subtle electronic sound design.
items.note: Good for testing product detail, camera cuts, reflections, and audio atmosphere.

items.title: Urban Night Car Scene
items.prompt: A sleek electric car crosses a rain-soaked downtown bridge at night. Cinematic tracking shot with tire spray, neon reflections, mist, realistic headlights, dramatic 4K lighting, low camera angle, synchronized rain and road ambience.
items.note: Good for testing motion, reflective surfaces, weather, and high-resolution output.

items.title: Creator Lifestyle Short
items.prompt: Vertical 9:16 video of a creator opening a compact travel camera in a bright apartment. Start with hands unboxing, cut to lens close-up, then show the creator smiling near a window. Natural handheld movement, warm daylight, soft room tone, social media pacing.
items.note: Good for testing short-form creator content and mobile framing.

items.title: Image-Guided Fashion Motion
items.prompt: Animate the uploaded fashion portrait into a graceful editorial video. Preserve the face, outfit color, pose, and background palette. Add a slow camera push-in, subtle fabric movement, soft hair motion, studio fan effect, elegant lighting, and clean cinematic texture.
items.note: Good for image-to-video tests where identity, wardrobe, and style must stay stable.

howToUse.title: How to Use Kling AI Video Generator

steps.title: Choose the starting mode
steps.desc: Use text-to-video for a new scene, or image-to-video when a product, person, composition, or first frame should guide the result.

steps.title: Write one clear scene direction
steps.desc: Describe the subject, action, camera movement, shot count, lighting, mood, sound, aspect ratio, and final use case.

steps.title: Select Kling settings
steps.desc: Pick duration, aspect ratio, resolution, and native audio options. Start with a shorter draft before spending more credits on high-resolution output.

steps.title: Generate and refine
steps.desc: Review motion stability, subject consistency, audio sync, and framing. Then simplify or expand the prompt based on what needs improvement.

troubleshooting.title: Improve Kling Video Results
troubleshooting.subtitle: Most weak video generations come from crowded prompts, unclear camera movement, or asking for too many actions in one short clip.

items.title: Motion looks unstable
items.desc: Reduce the prompt to one subject action and one camera move before adding extra shot detail.
items.prompt: Try: one slow push-in camera move, one centered subject, no rapid cuts.

items.title: Audio does not match
items.desc: When native audio is enabled, describe the exact sound source and remove background sounds you do not want.
items.prompt: Try: synchronized rain on metal, quiet city ambience, no music, no dialogue.

items.title: Reference details drift
items.desc: For image-to-video, call out the exact face, logo, product shape, clothing color, or camera angle that must remain stable.
items.prompt: Try: preserve the front label, silver cap, black sleeve, and three-quarter camera angle.

items.title: The clip feels generic
items.desc: Specify lens style, shot sequence, lighting, subject performance, and output format so Kling has a stronger direction.
items.prompt: Try: macro opening shot, low-angle tracking shot, final hero frame, cinematic product ad style.

faq.q: What is Kling AI Video Generator?
faq.a: It is a Toolaze video generator with Kling 3.0 selected by default. You can create videos from text prompts or reference images and adjust settings such as duration, aspect ratio, resolution, and native audio.

faq.q: Which Kling model does this page use?
faq.a: The page defaults to Kling 3.0. Toolaze also includes other Kling options in the broader video model selector when you want to compare speed, cost, native audio, or quality settings.
Yes. In Toolaze, Kling 3.0 supports text-to-video and image-to-video. Use image input when the subject, product, character, outfit, or first frame should guide the generated clip.
Kling 3.0 supports native audio at 720p and 1080p in the Toolaze model settings. Describe sound effects, ambience, dialogue cues, or music direction directly in the prompt when audio is enabled.

faq.q: How many credits does Kling use?
faq.a: Kling 3.0 starts at 60+ credits in Toolaze. The final credit use depends on duration, resolution, native audio, and the specific model option selected.

faq.q: How do I get better Kling video prompts?
faq.a: Write one clear subject, one main action, one camera direction, and the final format. Add lighting, sound, lens style, and shot sequence only after the core motion is clear.
